transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (Equinox CISO), Dave (Head of Infra), Sara (Product Security), Tom (Legal)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): Discussed encryption at rest/in-transit, BYOK options, HSM attestation, audit logging and SOC2 artifacts. Agreed next steps to share integration docs and run latency benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Marcus, our SE.
[00:00:07] Priya: Hi, thanks. I'm Priya, CISO at Equinox. We have Dave, Sara and Tom here. We have a fairly strict set of requirements around keys and audit.
[00:00:14] Marcus: Great, thanks. Today's agenda is encryption at rest and in transit, KMS and BYOK options, HSM support and a quick call out on audit logs and SOC2. We'll leave time for Q&A.
[00:00:25] Dave: To frame this, we run sensitive payment data and need customer keys for certain workloads, plus residency in eu-west-1; we do have corporate KMS in AWS.
[00:00:32] Lena: Understood. High level: Redwood supports TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit, and at-rest encryption by default. For customer-managed keys we support CMEK via cloud KMS providers and BYOK with HSM-backed keys, we also have private deployment options where keys never leave your VPC if needed.
[00:00:45] Sara: Are you able to confirm HSM vendor support? We need FIPS 140-2/3 and attestation.
[00:00:50] Marcus: Yes - we integrate with AWS KMS (CloudHSM), Azure Dedicated HSM, and we can do HashiCorp Vault integrations as well. For BYOK we support key wrap/unwarp flows using envelope encryption, so the data keys are stored encrypted by your master key in your KMS. We can provide HSM attestation and FIPS certs.
[00:01:10] Priya: When you say "keys never leave your VPC" - can you clarify? We're worried about Redwood accessing plaintext keys.
[00:01:16] Marcus: Good question. In our Private offering, the control plane can remain in Redwood's managed plane but the crypto operations use a gateway deployed in your VPC. You can deploy an HSM or point to your KMS endpoint so master key material is never transmitted to Redwood. For hosted customers we offer CMEK where Redwood integrates to your cloud KMS over a secure channel and only stores wrapped keys.
[00:01:38] Dave: For CMEK, what's the key lifecycle? Does Redwood rotate keys automatically or do we manage rotation?
[00:01:44] Lena: We support both. If you manage keys in your KMS, you control rotation and policies; Redwood can trigger key rewraps when you rotate. We also have managed rotation for platform keys if you prefer.
[00:01:55] Tom: From legal perspective, we need to ensure contract language about key custody and audit access. If keys are BYOK we want Redwood to provide logs proving they never unwrapped customer master keys.
[00:02:06] Marcus: Our audit logs include key usage events - wrap/unwrap, grant usage, which we can stream to your SIEM or S3 for retention. Logs capture request metadata, timestamp, and the calling principal. We can also provide an audit report for key operations scoped to the timeframe.
[00:02:22] Priya: What about latency? If the flow does an HSM unwrap on every request, token generation latency could spike.
[00:02:28] Marcus: Right - we use envelope encryption with data keys cached in a secure KV cache; unwraps happen only on key rotation or cache miss. For low-latency paths we recommend the KV cache + prefix caching; that reduces per-token unwrap frequency. For strict security profiles, you can set TTLs shorter but expect latency tradeoffs.
[00:02:46] Dave: Can you quantify unwrap time? What's the typical RTT to CloudHSM?
[00:02:50] Marcus: Typical cloud HSM unwrap is on the order of 50-150ms depending on region and provider. We have telemetry that shows the unwrap path can add 80-120ms median in eu-west due to network hops. That's why we do caching and local gateway options for private deployments to reduce that to single-digit ms. We can run benchmarks with your keys to show real numbers.
[00:03:12] Priya: Okay, that helps. Do you support hardware key import (BYOK import) or only remote key wrapping?
[00:03:18] Marcus: We support importing keys into CloudHSM/ADH for customers who want full ownership of key material. For BYOK with cloud KMS, typically you upload or import a key material package per provider docs - we can support the typical import flows and provide guidance.
[00:03:31] Sara: How do you handle backups and key escrow? If we lose Cmk?
[00:03:35] Lena: Key backups remain in your KMS provider; Redwood does not hold plaintext key backups. For private deployments you manage HSM backups per vendor best practices. We can document recommended recovery procedures.
[00:03:44] Tom: Regarding compliance, do you have SOC2 artifacts that show key management controls?
[00:03:49] Marcus: Yes. We have SOC2 Type II with control mappings that include cryptographic key management, access control, and logging. We'll attach the relevant sections and summaries; for deeper audits we can coordinate an NDA and provide redacted artifacts.
[00:04:01] Priya: Data residency - we need all eu customers' data and logs to stay in eu-west. How does Redwood guarantee that?
[00:04:08] Lena: We support region pinning for hosted and we have Private deployment so you can host in your VPC/region. For hosted we can ensure inference nodes and storage are in eu-west. We'll share a region topology and our data flow diagram.
[00:04:18] Dave: Is there any metadata that Redwood keeps that could leak residency? For example, support tickets or backups?
[00:04:23] Marcus: By default, support metadata is limited; PII is redacted and logs can be configured to redact. For strict customers we recommend Private deployment and restricting telemetry forwarding. We'll include the telemetry/data retention doc.
[00:04:34] Priya: About access control - RBAC and SSO - we need SCIM/SSO and ability to restrict key admin roles.
[00:04:40] Lena: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC in the Console. Key admin roles can be limited so only a small set of principals can request wrap/unwrap calls; and we can map those to your IdP groups.
[00:04:52] Sara: Do you support customer audit log export to our SIEM?
[00:04:55] Marcus: Yes - audit logs for crypto operations, access events, and admin changes can be exported via syslog, S3 sink, or direct SIEM connectors. Retention and format are configurable.
[00:05:05] Priya: On HSM attestation - can you provide mech to verify the HSM firmware and cert chain?
[00:05:10] Marcus: We can provide attestation docs and cert chain for supported HSM vendors; with private deployments the HSM is under your control and you can run attestation APIs directly. For cloud HSMs, we provide vendor attestation artifacts and we can show the certificate chain.
[00:05:23] Tom: For the contract clause, we want statement that Redwood never has access to plaintext CMKs for BYOK. Is that an existing template?
[00:05:29] Lena: We have contract language and an SOC2 addendum for customer-managed keys. We'll surface the template and we can iterate with your legal.
[00:05:36] Dave: Are there secrets in logs? Like do you log any tokens or keys by accident?
[00:05:40] Marcus: No - we mask sensitive fields in logs. We also have PII redaction in our logging pipeline. We'll include examples of log formats.
[00:05:48] Priya: If we do BYOK with CloudHSM, do you need any IAM role to perform unwraps? How's auth handled?
[00:05:54] Marcus: For cloud KMS integrations we require a minimal set of permissions (encrypt/decrypt, get public key, describe key) via an IAM role for Redwood's service account - or in Private you can deploy a local connector and no role is needed at Redwood side. We'll provide the exact IAM policy in the doc.
[00:06:07] Sara: One more on key rotation: can Redwood automatically rewrap objects when keys rotate? What's the migration pattern?
[00:06:13] Marcus: Yes - we perform a rewrap flow where we fetch the object data key, re-encrypt with the new master key, and persist. That can be done in bulk or on access. We also support versioned keys so you can roll forward safely.
[00:06:26] Priya: Any third-party auditors for crypto practices?
[00:06:29] Marcus: We have third-party attestation for SOC2, and our HSM vendors publish FIPS certifications. We also run internal crypto reviews and can provide summaries.
[00:06:38] Lena: Quick pause - any blockers we haven't covered?
[00:06:41] Priya: Two: we need the HSM attestation/cert chain and an estimate of latency impact per request in eu-west.
[00:06:48] Lena: We'll send attestation docs and run a latency benchmark with Marcus.
[00:06:52] Tom: Also, legal wants the BYOK contract language.
[00:06:55] Lena: We'll share our template.
[00:06:58] Dave: We might want a POC on a small subset of traffic to validate.
[00:07:01] Lena: Sounds good. Marcus, can you run the bench and help instrument?
[00:07:05] Marcus: Yep, I'll set up a 1-hour test window, capture unwrap latencies, token gen latency, and provide a spreadsheet.
[00:07:12] Priya: Anything else on encryption in transit? We require mutual TLS for some ingestion endpoints.
[00:07:17] Marcus: We support mTLS for private connectors and can require client certs on ingestion endpoints. For public hosted endpoints we use standard TLS with strong ciphers, and IP allow lists for extra control.
[00:07:28] Sara: Regarding retention, do audit logs get purged automatically? We need 7 year retention on certain events.
[00:07:33] Marcus: Retention configurable - we can export to your S3 and you control lifecycle policies. For retention beyond our default we offer an add-on for extended retention.
[00:07:44] Priya: Okay good. Can you also state whether Redwood stores any decrypted customer data at rest for analytics or debugging?
[00:07:51] Lena: We do not store customer data decrypted. We have a debug mode where customers can opt-in to share specific traces with redaction. Otherwise telemetry is anonymized.
[00:08:02] Tom: On a related note, if we request a support trace with keys, what's the process?
[00:08:06] Marcus: Typically, you create a support package leveraging a local decryption tool under your control; for hosted we do a limited signed trace where no plaintext keys are shared - it's a redactable bundle. We'll document the process.
[00:08:17] Priya: Great. Let's talk about next steps and timelines.
[00:08:20] Lena: We'll send the KMS/BYOK integration diagram, HSM attestation artifacts, and the IAM policy for cloud KMS. Marcus will schedule the latency benchmark using your eu-west keys. Tom will get contract language to Lena.
[00:08:33] Dave: Target timeline - we'd like POC in next 2-3 weeks.
[00:08:37] Lena: We'll aim to schedule the bench next week and share docs in 3 business days.
[00:08:43] Priya: Thanks, that's helpful.
[00:08:46] Lena: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and calendar invites.
[00:08:50] [Meeting end]
